summary:
Delaware is a state of the United States and stands under the US national framework, which the national record and the parent bundle carry. What follows is Delaware's own law and practice.

A national trans legal risk assessment dated July 2026 places Delaware in its Low-Risk States group, alongside Arizona, Maine, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Wisconsin and the District of Columbia. The assessment defines that group as jurisdictions that largely refrain from targeting transgender adults without specialising in their protection.

Delaware has no state ban on transgender people using public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity. The Movement Advancement Project equality map, which tracks such bans state by state, records no such ban for Delaware.

Since 2013, Delaware law prohibits discrimination on the basis of actual or perceived gender identity in employment, housing, public accommodations and other areas. The statute is SB 97, which passed the Senate 11-7 on 6 June 2013, passed the House 24-17 with amendments, passed the Senate on amendments 11-9 on 18 June, was signed the following day and took effect immediately.

Since 2013 Delaware also imposes additional penalties for a violent crime motivated by the victim's actual or perceived gender identity.

Gender markers on Delaware documents are changed without a surgical requirement. Transgender people may change the legal gender on state-issued identification on the signed statement of a licensed medical provider alone. Since 11 February 2017 sex reassignment surgery has not been an explicit requirement for an amended birth certificate; the applicant supplies a signed affidavit of surgical, hormonal, psychological or other treatment appropriate for gender transition. As of April 2020 Delaware did not offer an X marker on driver's licences, and no later source in this record addresses the point.

Since 26 March 2016 Delaware has prohibited discrimination based on gender identity within insurance contracts, including coverage of sex reassignment surgery.

Delaware bans conversion therapy on minors. SB 65, introduced 26 April 2017 and signed and effective 23 July 2018 as Laws of Delaware 81:340, defines conversion therapy to include practices seeking to change gender identity, behaviours or gender expressions, and makes it unprofessional conduct subject to discipline for physicians, nurses, mental health and chemical dependency professionals, psychologists and clinical social workers who perform it on a minor or refer a minor out of state for it. The statute also bars the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families from performing or recommending it for a minor.

Same-sex marriage has been legal in Delaware since 1 July 2013, with conversion of existing civil unions to marriages; civil unions carrying the rights, benefits, protections and responsibilities of married persons had been available since 1 January 2012.

HB142, which would formally repeal the common-law gay and trans panic defence and ban its use, was introduced in May 2023 and passed both houses of the Legislature in June 2023. The record does not document the Governor's subsequent action.
tangentialFactors:
The July 2026 assessment's framing matters for expectations on the ground: Delaware is grouped with states that do not target transgender adults but are also not described as specialising in their protection, so the low-risk designation reflects absence of hostile legislation rather than a dedicated protective regime.

Delaware's protections rest on statute and executive action of long standing, dating from 2009 and 2013, and the record shows no Delaware legislative session in this inventory pursuing restrictions on transgender people. The turbulence visible in this inventory is confined to bills awaiting executive action rather than measures in force.

Two Delaware bills sat unresolved at the last date documented here: HB142 on the panic defence, passed June 2023 with no sourced outcome, and a May 2021 bill repealing a single-orientation loophole in the state's anti-discrimination law, also passed with the Governor's action unsourced.
localsOnly:
Delaware Executive Order Eight, signed 11 August 2009, extended anti-discrimination safeguards to state employees and applicants for state employment on the basis of gender identity and reauthorised the Governor's Council on Equal Employment Opportunity with a charge to foster an inclusive environment among executive-branch employees.

A law signed 25 June 2015 and effective immediately allows inmates to access and change the name on birth certificates to reflect gender identity; previously inmates could change names only on religious grounds.

In January 2025 Governor Hall-Long signed an Executive Order creating Delaware's LGBTQ+ Commission.

Delaware's sexual-orientation protections run parallel to its gender-identity rules: discrimination based on actual or perceived sexual orientation has been prohibited since 2009, additional penalties for orientation-motivated violent crime have applied since 2001, and same-sex sexual activity has been legal since 1 January 1973 following repeal of the sodomy law in July 1972.
outOfScopeNotes:
The Movement Advancement Project equality map page cited for Delaware's facilities position was not retrievable at the archived URL (HTTP 404). The claim that the underlying map records no bathroom or facilities ban for Delaware is carried from the source inventory and remains unverified against the live page.

No Delaware-specific policy on the placement of transgender inmates in state custody is documented in this inventory. Federal prisoner-housing policy is addressed at the national layer.

The absence of an X marker on Delaware driver's licences is stated as of April 2020; no later source in this record confirms whether that remains the case.

The final status of HB142 is unresolved: the inventory records passage of both houses in June 2023 but no sourced gubernatorial signature or veto.
